topic: Important Days and Dates: National and Global
description: Direct questions regarding important National and International Days are frequently asked in the 'Static GK' section of competitive exams. This study guide categorizes crucial days related to historical events, health, and the environment for rapid revision.

sections.title: Important Days from January to March
sections.description: Major national and international awareness days observed in the first quarter of the year.

key_associations.extra_info: Commemorates the return of Mahatma Gandhi to India from South Africa in 1915.
Celebrated to commemorate the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.
Marks the discovery of the 'Raman Effect' by Indian physicist Sir C.V. Raman in 1928.
A global day celebrating the social, economic, cultural, and political achievements of women.
Highlights the importance of freshwater and advocates for the sustainable management of freshwater resources.

sections.title: Important Days from April to June
sections.description: Key global days focusing on health, environment, and labor observed in the second quarter.

key_associations.extra_info: Marks the anniversary of the founding of the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1948.
An annual event to demonstrate global support for environmental protection.
Honors the struggles, rights, and contributions of workers and the working class worldwide.
The United Nations' principal vehicle for encouraging global awareness and action for the environment.
Celebrates the physical, mental, and spiritual practices of Yoga, originating from ancient India.

sections.title: Important Days from July to September
sections.description: Crucial days associated with sports, population issues, and environmental conservation in the third quarter.

key_associations.extra_info: Focuses attention on the urgency and importance of global population issues.
Commemorates the birth anniversary of Indian hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand.
Celebrated in India on the birth anniversary of the second President, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.
Commemorates the signing of the Montreal Protocol in 1987 for the preservation of the ozone layer.

sections.title: Important Days from October to December
sections.description: Major human rights, health, and United Nations-related days observed in the final quarter.

key_associations.extra_info: Declared by the UN to mark the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.
Marks the anniversary of the entry into force of the UN Charter in 1945.
Dedicated to raising awareness of the AIDS pandemic caused by the spread of HIV infection.
Commemorates the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights by the UNGA in 1948.
Observed in India on the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

sections.title: Historical Context of Important Days
sections.description: Specific national days based on major events in Indian history.

historical_events.significance: Celebrated to mark the birth anniversary of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, officially declared by the Government of India in 2021.
Commemorates the anniversary of the day Indira Gandhi took the oath as the first woman Prime Minister of India in 1966.
Marks the formal adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly in 1949.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: Direct, one-liner facts related to important days frequently asked in exams.

important_facts.fact: The 'Trinity of 22' is often used by students to remember three consecutive nature-related days: World Water Day (22 March), Earth Day (22 April), and International Day for Biological Diversity (22 May).
Kargil Vijay Diwas is celebrated on 26 July every year, marking the success of Operation Vijay and India's victory over Pakistani forces in the 1999 Kargil War.
The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) recognized 21 June as the International Day of Yoga in 2014, following a proposal strongly advocated by India.
National Panchayati Raj Day is celebrated on 24 April because the landmark 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act came into force on this day in 1993.
National Voters' Day is celebrated on 25 January to mark the foundation day of the Election Commission of India, which was established on 25 January 1950.
